title: Subnet role allocator and egress-healing Terraform module for private deployments
creator: Aisha Desai
description: Create a reusable, AZ-aware Terraform module that allocates subnet role profiles (control/serving/management) and implements an egress-healing controller for NAT/IGW endpoints and VPC endpoints. The module must support safe in-place upgrades, automated health checks and recovery workflows, and explicit rollout controls for Private (VPC) deployments used by Redwood Private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes role-based subnet creation (roles: control, serving, management, shared-services) with per-role route table templates and tags
Supports both centralized egress (single NAT/egress cluster) and distributed egress (per-AZ NAT or IGW) via a single variable toggle

Creates Gateway/Gateway-like resources (IGW, NAT Gateways or egress instances) and VPC endpoints (S3 Gateway, DynamoDB Gateway, interface endpoints) with idempotent names suitable for tfstate upgrades
Includes automated health checks (synthetic probe + route table blackhole detection) and an egress-healing null_resource or Lambda hook to trigger replacement or failover
Upgrade path documented: minor safe changes (new tags/outputs) do not replace critical resources; major changes provide migration scripts and example tfstate commands
Module has a CI terratest suite covering plan/apply/destroy in a sandbox, and a canary upgrade job that runs in our staging account
Module includes clear IAM least-privilege example policies for Private control plane to operate and for customer-managed KMS integrations
implementation_notes: Design will define subnet_role map variable: {name_pattern, cidr_template, availability_zones, route_table_settings, nat_preference}
Use for_each on az-aware subnet constructions to keep resource addresses stable across AZ additions; avoid count when names/enumeration may change
Provide opt-in ephemeral NAT controller using Lambda+autoscaling to allocate small nat gateways and prefer IGW when cost/perf tradeoffs favor it
Expose route table modules for per-role route priorities: internal peering routes, egress routes, endpoint routes with explicit propagation flags
Add lifecycle rules (prevent_destroy, create_before_destroy) for gateway and endpoint resources where feasible; document when replacement is unavoidable
Implement a provider_alias pattern to support cross-account endpoint creation for Private control plane versus customer VPC resources
upgrade_strategy: Semantic versioning for module with clear migration notes in CHANGELOG.md
Minor releases only introduce optional outputs/inputs; patch releases only change docs and tests
For breaking changes, ship a v2 migration guide with terraform state mv examples and automated migration script in 'scripts/terraform-migrate-v2.sh'
CI runs a planned drift detection job that checks for resources with replacement in plan for the upgrade commit; block merge if replacements exceed threshold
Support a canary rollout variable (canary_account, canary_subnet_ids) to apply new module in one account/region before full rollout
health_checks: Route table blackhole detector: periodic Lambda that queries route tables and tests reachability to known egress IPs; emits CloudWatch metrics
Endpoint health synthetic probes: VPC interface endpoint ping/HTTPS probe using ENI-attached test runner in each AZ
NAT latencies and packet drop alarms from VPC Flow Logs aggregated to CloudWatch metrics
Terraform drift detection: nightly plan against last-applied vars and alert if drift present
Automated remediation actions: either create replacement NAT in same AZ or switch route table to a standby egress gateway depending on configured policy
testing_plan: Unit tests: terraform validate + static check with tflint rules and custom checks for lifecycle meta-arguments
Integration: terratest suite that creates a 3-AZ VPC, provisions subnets and endpoints, runs the synthetic probes, and verifies route table failover
Upgrade tests: staged upgrade from module v1.6 -> v2.0 in sandbox using scripted tfstate migration; verify no service-impacting replacements
Chaos scenario: simulate AZ NAT loss and assert egress-healing workflow restores connectivity within SLO
Security test: IAM policy scanner and KMS key access checks for endpoint and control-plane roles
